articles.title: Stock Market Today Live Updates: Where are NSE Nifty50 and BSE Sensex headed?
articles.full_text: Indian equity markets are expected to open on a flat to mildly negative note, with Gift Nifty trading around 24,650, down by 14 points, indicating subdued opening cues for domestic indices. Global markets remain cautiously positive as investors continue to assess the latest U.S. corporate earnings and the outlook for interest rates following last week's Federal Reserve policy decision. With no major negative global triggers overnight, domestic markets are likely to witness stock-specific action while participants closely monitor global cues and upcoming macroeconomic developments.In the previous session on 3rd August 2026, Nifty 50 ended at 24,774, gaining 390.70 points (+1.60%) after witnessing broad-based buying throughout the session. The index opened with a strong gap-up at 24,572 and remained largely range-bound before a sharp late-session rally propelled it to close at the day's high. Technically, the formation of a strong bullish candlestick and a decisive close above the 200-day EMA reinforce the strengthening long-term trend. The RSI improved to 66.87, while India VIX remained at a comfortable 11.92, indicating healthy momentum with controlled volatility.From a technical perspective, 24,450–24,500 is expected to act as the immediate support zone, while 24,750–24,800 remains the key resistance area. A sustained move above the resistance band could extend the ongoing rally towards higher levels, whereas any decline towards support is likely to attract fresh buying interest and keep the broader outlook positive. Rupee strengthened for a sixth consecutive session, closing 12 paise higher at 95.31 against the US dollar. The domestic currency was supported by a sharp decline in global crude oil prices, a softer dollar and sustained foreign institutional inflows. During the session, rupee traded within a narrow range of 95.11 to 95.34 before ending higher than its previous close of 95.43 against the US dollar. Forex traders said easing geopolitical tensions following the postponement of possible US military action against Iran improved global risk appetite, encouraging buying in emerging market currencies. According to Mirae Asset Sharekhan analyst Anuj Choudhary, lower crude prices and optimism surrounding potential US-Iran dialogue boosted the rupee, although any renewed tensions could limit further appreciation. Market experts attributed the rally largely to falling crude oil prices, easing geopolitical concerns and improving foreign investor sentiment. Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder and CEO of HST Wealth, said broad-based buying emerged after tensions in the Middle East softened and global oil prices corrected sharply, improving investor confidence. Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments, noted that lower crude prices eased worries around inflation and corporate profitability, while a stronger rupee and renewed FII inflows further supported domestic markets. However, he cautioned that elevated US bond yields remain a key risk for emerging markets. Analysts also observed that improving valuations and better corporate earnings have helped foreign investors turn net buyers of Indian equities after several months of selling. Indian benchmark equity indices ended higher as investors cheered a sharp decline in crude oil prices and signs of easing geopolitical tensions in West Asia. BSE Sensex climbed 544.39 points, or 0.70%, to close at 78,639.03, while NSE Nifty advanced 390.70 points, or 1.60%, to settle at 24,774.30. It marked the fourth straight session of gains for domestic equities, with technology, services, industrials, FMCG and metal stocks leading the advance. InterGlobe Aviation, Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, ITC and Axis Bank were among the biggest gainers, while Sun Pharma, Bharti Airtel and Tata Steel lagged. Broader markets also participated in the rally, with the BSE MidCap and SmallCap indices ending in positive territory. Investors also welcomed continued foreign institutional buying, reflecting improving confidence in Indian equities.

articles.title: From a rented garage to a global biotech giant: How Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw built Biocon after being told women couldn't brew beer
articles.description: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw’s journey from aspiring brewmaster to Biocon founder shows how setbacks can become opportunities. After being denied brewing jobs because of gender bias, she launched Biocon in 1978 with Rs 10,000 in a rented garage. The company grew into a global biopharmaceutical leader serving over 120 countries. Her story highlights the value of education, resilience and scientific thinking, while demonstrating that success is defined by innovation, perseverance and giving back to society.
